meta.title: Word Lists – Master Index
meta.description: Complete index of all JSON word list files for the language learning app. Three categories: Curriculum Learning, Word Group Learning, and Theme Learning.

1_curriculum_learning.label: Curriculum Learning
1_curriculum_learning.description: Official and curriculum-aligned vocabulary lists based on Cambridge YLE exams and the French Éducation Nationale programme for English.

cambridge_yle.label: Cambridge English for Young Learners (YLE)
cambridge_yle.description: Three levels of the Cambridge YLE suite, for learners aged 6–12. Based on the official Cambridge wordlists for exams from 2018.

files.title: Cambridge YLE – Pre-A1 Starters
files.notes: Core vocabulary for the youngest learners. Organised by topic (animals, body, clothes, colours, family, food, home, numbers, school, sports, time, toys, transport).

files.title: Cambridge YLE – A1 Movers
files.notes: Words ADDITIONAL to the Starters list. Use alongside starters_pre_a1.json for the full Movers vocabulary set.

files.title: Cambridge YLE – A2 Flyers
files.notes: Words ADDITIONAL to the Starters and Movers lists. Roughly equivalent to Cambridge A2 Key for Schools but with child-appropriate topics.

brevet_bac.label: French Curriculum – Brevet and Bac Aligned
brevet_bac.description: English vocabulary aligned with the French Éducation Nationale programme for English as a foreign language (LV1/LV2), covering collège (Brevet) and lycée (Bac) levels.

files.title: Brevet-Aligned English Vocabulary
files.notes: Eight thematic areas from the French collège English curriculum: identity, school, the English-speaking world, technology, environment, myths and heroes, sport/health, arts/media.

files.title: Bac-Aligned English Vocabulary
files.notes: The five thematic axes of the French lycée English Bac programme (2021 reform): L'art de vivre ensemble, Territoire et mémoire, Expressions et représentations, Innovations scientifiques, Rencontres avec l'autre.

2_word_group_learning.label: Word Group Learning
2_word_group_learning.description: AI-generated vocabulary by word class, organised by CEFR level. Each file covers nouns, verbs, adjectives, adverbs, prepositions of time and place, connectives, and idioms.

3_theme_learning.label: Theme Learning
3_theme_learning.description: AI-generated thematic vocabulary lists, organised by CEFR level and topic. Seven core themes plus three specialist topics.

specialist_files.label: Specialist Topics (no fixed level)
specialist_files.description: These lists are not tied to a specific CEFR level. They cover professional/specialist registers needed regardless of age or exam.

files.title: Business and Finance Terms
files.notes: Includes professional phrases and business idioms.

files.title: Medical and Psychological Terms
files.notes: Language learning resource only — not medical advice.

files.title: Practical English – Real-World Phrases
files.notes: Full phrases rather than isolated words. Ideal for travel and real-world use. British English primary, with US variants noted.

design_notes.json_structure: Each file uses a consistent meta block (title, level, source, description) followed by categorised word objects with 'word' and 'type' fields as minimum, plus optional 'example', 'notes', 'translation_hint', and 'meaning' fields.

word_object_fields.type: Grammatical type: noun, verb, adjective, adverb, expression, phrasal verb, etc. (recommended)
word_object_fields.notes: Clarifications, e.g. plural forms, UK/US variants (optional)
word_object_fields.meaning: Used for idioms to explain the figurative meaning (optional)
word_object_fields.translation_hint: A simple gloss, not a full translation (optional, used at A1/A2)

design_notes.cambridge_yle_usage: The three YLE files are cumulative. Starters is the base level. Movers words should be used alongside Starters. Flyers words should be used alongside both Starters and Movers.
design_notes.practical_english_note: The practical_english.json file uses a 'phrases' array (not 'words') with 'phrase' and 'use' fields, given its communicative rather than lexical focus.
